articles.body: The Nifty 50 bounced back with a half-percent rally and closed above the previous day’s high, despite facing pressure at higher levels on May 4. A favourable election outcome in West Bengal and better-than-expected Q4 earnings supported market sentiment. Momentum indicators remained mixed, with a sideways trend observed in the RSI. A decisive move above 24,300 could potentially open further upside towards the 24,600–24,800 levels in the near term. Any failure to sustain these higher levels may lead to further consolidation or minor weakness in the short term, with support seen at 23,800, according to experts. articles.body: Both FIIs and DIIs were net buyers on May 4, provisional exchange data shows. Foreign investors (FIIs/FPIs) net bought shares worth Rs 2,836 crore, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) net bought shares worth Rs 4,764 crore, during the trading session.    DIIs purchased shares worth Rs 19,516 crore and sold shares worth Rs 14,752 crore. In contrast, FIIs bought shares worth Rs 19,660 crore but sold shares totalling Rs 16,825 crore.    For the year so far, FIIs have been net sellers of shares worth Rs 2.36 lakh crore and DIIs net bought shares worth Rs 2.95 lakh crore .        Market view    At close, the Sensex was up 355.90 points or 0.46 percent at 77,269.40, and the Nifty was up 121.75 points or 0.51 percent at 24,119.30.    On today's market, Ajit Mishra – SVP, Research, Religare Broking,  noted that during the day, the initial upmove was primarily driven by cooling crude oil prices following signs of geopolitical relief in the Middle East, which supported global sentiment. &quot;Strong monthly auto sales data and buying in select heavyweights further aided the rally. However, intermittent volatility persisted due to ongoing uncertainty around US–Iran negotiations, a weak rupee, and state election results, which capped the upside,&quot; he said.    Mishra added that indications suggest a continuation of consolidation in the index, given the pressure in key sectors like banking and IT, along with crude oil prices remaining elevated. &quot;Immediate support is placed at 23,800, followed by 23,500, while the upside appears capped in the 24,600–24,800 zone. Traders are advised to maintain a sector- and theme-specific approach and prefer hedged strategies until clearer directional signals emerge,&quot; he said. articles.body: Shares of ideaForge Technology on Monday hit the upper circuit limit of 20 percent after the drone technology firm reported a profit for the March quarter.    The stock touched a fresh 52-week high of Rs 731 per share on the NSE. It has been on a gaining streak for the past five sessions and has risen 42 percent during the period.    The scrip opened with a gap-up of 16.55 percent in the session.    Buying interest strengthened after the company reported a net profit of Rs 60 crore for the quarter, against a net loss of Rs 26 crore in the corresponding period last year.    Revenue rose sharply to Rs 141 crore from Rs 20 crore a year ago. On a sequential basis, the company’s topline also recorded strong growth.    Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs 62 crore for the quarter, compared to an EBITDA loss of Rs 22 crore in the year-ago period. Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to strengthen the capital base of its subsidiary, Si Creva, to support future funding requirements and for general corporate purposes.    Founded in 2016, the company operates the digital lending platform Kissht, which provides credit solutions to young consumers in the mass market segment. articles.title: With BJP's historic win in West Bengal, markets see fresh hope for Eastern revival
articles.snippet: Ongoing election developments kept sentiment mixed across markets, though expectations of policy stability provided some support. Thus, resulting in a cautiously optimistic near-term outlook.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Ongoing election developments kept sentiment mixed across markets, though expectations of policy stability provided some support. Thus, resulting in a cautiously optimistic near-term outlook.
articles.body: The BJP’s strong performance in West Bengal has delivered a major political shift, ending nearly 50 years of non-BJP rule in the state. This in turn is raising expectations for markets, of better Centre-State cooperation and faster development. After nearly 49 years of the state often being in opposition to the Centre, people are hopeful about a “double engine” government delivering faster progress.    Madhavi Arora, Chief Economist at Emkay Global, expressed her thoughts on the win. “A BJP win in West Bengal is a major political shift, given the state’s long history of non-BJP dominance, from the Left Front era to the current rule of Mamata Banerjee led TMC. This validates the Modi+Shah policy strategy of welfare and national security. The implications would ripple well beyond the state. Expansion of BJP’s eastern footprint in a big state ahead of next year’s UP election strengthen its narrative of becoming a truly pan-India party,&quot; she said.    Arora is hopeful of this win accelerating administrative clearances for central schemes in the state, with better Centre-State alignment. &quot;It could be positive for the State’s industrial policy &amp;amp; manufacturing in the medium term. However, state’s fiscal discipline vs populist spending would become a key test in the near term,&quot; she added.    Feroz Azeez, Joint CEO at Anand Rathi Wealth, sees the verdict as largely positive from an economic angle. He pointed out that the sresultant Centre-State coordination will speed up project execution, make industrialisation easier, boost infrastructure (including ports), improve fiscal prudence, and enhance law and order perception — all critical for manufacturing and logistics.    Analysts are hopeful that after West Bengal having lagged national per capita income for decade, the latest election results should help the state contribute more to national growth after years of being out of sync.    Azeez also noted long-term political benefits, saying a stronger BJP performance in the state could help the NDA win more of West Bengal’s 42 Lok Sabha seats in 2029, reinforcing policy continuity that markets favour. On the broader outlook, he remains constructive and expects Nifty to deliver above-median returns, with 27,000 to 28,000 levels possible by year-end, supported by strong domestic fund flows.    At closing today, the Nifty recovered from an intraday dip to cross the 24,000 mark in the final hours of trade as investors cheered the outcome. However, gains remained modest amid global uncertainties.    Ajit Mishra, Senior Vice President – Research at Religare Broking, said the election result is providing short-term positive sentiment but its impact is usually limited. “State election outcomes typically influence the market for a day or two before fundamentals take over,” he highlighted while adding that elevated crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions continue to weigh on sentiment.    With Banking and IT sectors under pressure, a strong directional move higher looks difficult in the near term. Mishra expects the Nifty to trade in a 600 to 800 point range, with immediate support at 23,800 and resistance near 24,500 to 24,600.    Key expectations include continuity (and possible expansion) of popular welfare schemes, quicker completion of stalled metro and road projects, a fresh industrial policy with attractive incentives, and attracting back investments that had moved to states like Odisha. There is also hope for more Global Capability Centres, a facelift for Kolkata, and a revival in the local startup ecosystem. Infrastructure, cement, capital goods and manufacturing, are expected to see progress on expectations of faster project clearances and new incentives. While Banking shall be tracked for potential pickup in credit growth.

articles.title: Sebi proposes changes to SDI rules to facilitate growth in listed securitisation market
articles.snippet: In its consultation paper, the regulator suggested exempting entities regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from the requirement that limits exposure to a single obligor in the asset pool, thereby enabling the listing of single-asset securitisation transactions.
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: In its consultation paper, the regulator suggested exempting entities regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from the requirement that limits exposure to a single obligor in the asset pool, thereby enabling the listing of single-asset securitisation transactions.
articles.body: Markets regulator Sebi on Monday proposed a series of changes to norms governing securitised debt instruments (SDIs), including allowing single-asset securitisation by RBI-regulated entities, winding up of securitisation transactions and easing certain structural restrictions to boost market development.    Besides, the regulator suggested shifting the responsibility for periodic disclosures on the underlying asset pool's performance from the originator to the servicer. The regulator also proposed changes to the composition of the board of trustees for special-purpose distinct entities.    The proposed changes are aimed at harmonising Sebi's framework with RBI regulations and facilitating growth in the listed securitisation market.    In its consultation paper, the regulator suggested exempting entities regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from the requirement that limits exposure to a single obligor in the asset pool, thereby enabling the listing of single-asset securitisation transactions.    Sebi said the current rule, which caps exposure to any single obligor at 25 per cent of the pool, was aimed at preventing concentration risk but has restricted the listing of SDIs backed by single assets, even though such structures are permitted under the RBI's framework.    Additionally, the regulator has proposed replacing the requirement of winding up securitisation schemes in case of suspension or cancellation of a trustee's registration with the appointment of a new trustee, citing inconsistencies with RBI regulations that do not permit unwinding of such transactions.    In another proposal, the regulator recommended removing restrictions that currently bar securitisation transactions between an originator and an SPDE belonging to the same group, provided the originator is regulated by the RBI.    The regulator has also proposed shifting the responsibility of periodic disclosures on the performance of the underlying asset pool from the originator to the servicer, which may or may not be the originator. This is aimed at ensuring timely and accurate information flow to investors, given that the servicer handles the collection and monitoring of receivables.    Further, Sebi has suggested changes to the composition of the board of trustees of special purpose distinct entities (SPDEs). For RBI-regulated originators, it proposed limiting representation on the SPDE board to one member without veto powers, aligning with RBI norms to maintain arm's length transactions.    The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has invited public comments on the proposals till May 25.

articles.title: Jio BlackRock Mutual Fund files SID for Prism Hybrid Long - Short Fund
articles.snippet: The fund carries a minimum investment threshold of Rs 10 lakh for most investors, positioning it toward high-net-worth individuals and sophisticated participants. It has been categorised under a moderate risk band and benchmarked against a hybrid equity-debt index to reflect its balanced mandate.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News

articles.body: Jio BlackRock Mutual Fund has filed its Scheme Information Document (SID) for its first specialized investment offering, marking a formal entry into India’s competitive asset management space. The filing introduces the Prism Hybrid Long-Short Fund under its Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) platform, an interval strategy designed to combine equity, debt, and derivative exposures in a single portfolio.    The proposed fund aims to deliver long-term capital appreciation along with income generation by investing across a diversified mix of asset classes, including equity and equity-related instruments, fixed income securities, and derivative-based strategies such as arbitrage and hedging. According to the document, the strategy will typically allocate 35–75% to equities and 25–65% to debt instruments, while allowing limited short exposure through derivatives.    Structured as an interval fund, the product will allow subscriptions on a daily basis while offering redemptions twice a week, a format that balances liquidity with portfolio stability. Units are expected to be listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, enabling secondary market participation alongside periodic redemption windows.    According to the fund house, the scheme will use advanced analytics and global investment technology, including data-driven signals and portfolio optimization tools, reflecting the influence of partner BlackRock. The strategy also incorporates derivative techniques such as merger arbitrage, collar strategies, and market-neutral positioning to manage risk and generate returns across market cycles.    The fund carries a minimum investment threshold of Rs 10 lakh for most investors, positioning it toward high-net-worth individuals and sophisticated participants. It has been categorized under a moderate risk band and benchmarked against a hybrid equity-debt index to reflect its balanced mandate.    At a recent event in Mumbai, CEO Sid Swaminathan announced that the AMC which had been using a digital only, direct to investors approach will will begin offering its upcoming SIF products through both regular plans and direct plans, a major expansion of its distribution approach. articles.title: NSE launches electronic gold receipts to formalise India’s gold market
articles.snippet: According to NSE, the launch is expected to enable efficient price discovery, improve market participation and enhance trust among stakeholders including jewellers, refiners, traders and institutional investors.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: According to NSE, the launch is expected to enable efficient price discovery, improve market participation and enhance trust among stakeholders including jewellers, refiners, traders and institutional investors.
articles.body: The National Stock Exchange of India on Monday announced the launch of Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs), a new segment aimed at bringing transparency, efficiency and formalisation to India’s vast gold market. The exchange said the initiative is designed to bridge the gap between physical gold and financial markets by offering a regulated, secure and technology-driven platform for trading the precious metal.    EGRs are dematerialised securities representing ownership of physical gold stored in Securities and Exchange Board of India-accredited vaults and held electronically through depositories, enabling seamless trading within the formal financial system.    Speaking at the IMC Capital Market Conference being held at NSE, MD &amp;amp; CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan said, “It gives immense pleasure to us to announce the introduction of electronic receipts on NSE today,” adding that the EGR segment had gone live and had already seen the creation of its first receipt.    He thanked SEBI for its “planning and wholehearted support” and compared the move to the dematerialisation of equity shares in the 1990s.    “By enabling gold to be held in dematerialized form as EGR and traded seamlessly on a regulated platform, many of the challenges associated with physical handling, storage and parity assurance can be addressed,” Chauhan said.    According to NSE, the launch is expected to enable efficient price discovery, improve market participation and enhance trust among stakeholders including jewellers, refiners, traders and institutional investors.    The exchange also confirmed the successful dematerialisation of a 1,000-gram gold bar into an EGR, signalling the operational readiness of the framework for delivery-backed trading.    Chauhan further said EGRs would help make markets more transparent, efficient and globally competitive while enabling more productive use of gold as a non-financial asset.    In addition, he announced the launch of PARVA (Past Risk and Return Verification Agency), a joint initiative with CARE Ratings, describing it as a first-of-its-kind SEBI-driven framework to verify performance claims of portfolio managers and algorithmic traders. articles.title: Nifty likely to extend pullback to 24,600 in short-term as long as it stays above 23,950, say analysts
articles.snippet: Broader markets outperformed, with midcap and smallcap indices rising about 0.8 per cent each.
articles.author: Paras Bisht
articles.description: Broader markets outperformed, with midcap and smallcap indices rising about 0.8 per cent each.
articles.body: The equity benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty settled higher on Monday after a volatile session, supported by gains in select heavyweight stocks amid mixed global cues.    After a firm opening, the Nifty pared gains during the day but managed to settle in positive territory, rising 121.75 points or 0.51 percent to close at 24,119.30.    The Sensex advanced 355.90 points or 0.46 percent to end at 77,269.40. During intra-day trade, it had surged 997.25 points or 1.29 percent to 77,910.75.    Analysts said the Nifty may extend its pullback towards the 24,600 level in the short term, provided it holds above the 23,950 mark.    Immediate resistance for the index is seen in the 24,250–24,300 zone. A sustained move above this range could push the Nifty towards 24,450 and then 24,600 in the near term, said Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities.    On the downside, immediate support is placed in the 23,980–23,950 zone, he added.    Ajit Mishra, Senior Vice President (Research) at Religare Broking, said support for the index is placed at 23,800, followed by 23,500, while the upside is likely to remain capped in the 24,600–24,800 range.    Sectorally, realty, metals and pharma stocks led the gains, while banking and IT stocks remained subdued. Broader markets outperformed, with midcap and smallcap indices rising about 0.8 per cent each.    Bank Nifty also mirrored the trend and formed a thin-bodied candle with an upper wick, indicating resistance at higher levels. The index faced selling pressure near its 20-day exponential moving average, signalling weakness in the near term.    Immediate support for Bank Nifty is placed in the 54,400–54,300 zone. A break below this level could drag the index towards 53,900 and 53,500 in the short term. On the upside, the 55,300–55,400 range is expected to act as immediate resistance, Shah said. articles.body: Indian equity markets staged a strong rebound on Monday (May 4), recovering from Thursday’s sharp sell-off, supported by broad-based buying amid robust April auto sales data, easing crude oil prices, and positive political cues.    The benchmarks opened the week on a firm footing, with the Nifty 50 climbing close to the 24,300 mark in early trade. However, mid-session profit booking pared a significant portion of the intraday gains, though the index managed to hold above the 24,100 level at close.    At close, the Sensex was up 355.90 points or 0.46 percent at 77,269.40, and the Nifty was up 121.75 points or 0.51 percent at 24,119.30.    Meanwhile, broader markets remained supportive, with the Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices rising about 0.5% each.    Also Read: Sequential SIP growth slows despite strong annual gains; large AMCs stay ahead    Among the top gainers on the Nifty were Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, Adani Enterprises, Eicher Motors, Reliance Industries, and Jio Financial. On the flip side, laggards included Bharti Airtel, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, and Tata Consultancy Services.    On the sectoral front, metal, realty, infrastructure, and pharma indices gained around 0.5–1%, while IT, media, and PSU Bank indices ended lower. Click to View More    In stock-specific action, shares of Bharat Heavy Electricals surged 7.5% after the company reported a sharp jump in its Q4 earnings. Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone gained 5.5% following a 15% year-on-year increase in cargo volumes to 43.1 MMT.    On the downside, Sun TV Network declined 5.5% amid a ruling party setback in Tamil Nadu, while Kotak Mahindra Bank slipped 3% despite reporting better-than-expected Q4 earnings. articles.title: US stock futures fall, crude oil jumps over 5% after reports of attack on US warship in Strait of Hormuz
articles.snippet: US stock futures erased early gains and turned lower while Brent crude surged over 5 percent after reports of an attack on a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating Middle East tensions. The risk-off move also dragged European stocks into the red and lifted the dollar.
articles.author: Shaleen Agrawal
articles.description: US stock futures erased early gains and turned lower while Brent crude surged over 5 percent after reports of an attack on a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating Middle East tensions. The risk-off move also dragged European stocks into the red and lifted the dollar.
articles.body: US stock futures turned sharply lower on Monday after reports of escalating tensions in the Middle East, including claims that a US warship was hit in the Strait of Hormuz. On the other hand, crude oil prices surged amid fears of supply disruption.    Contracts linked to the S&amp;amp;P 500 and Nasdaq 100 fell about 0.5 percent each as of around 6:15 am EDT (3:45 pm IST), reversing earlier gains. Dow Jones futures were trading down 0.8 percent. GIFT Nifty futures fell around 0.5 percent, or about 115 points, to 24,090.    The decline in US futures came after Iran’s Fars news agency reported that two missiles had struck a US warship that had ignored warnings. Iran’s army separately claimed it had prevented US warships from entering the Strait of Hormuz.    Brent crude prices spiked sharply, rising more than 5 percent to trade around $114 per barrel, as the developments heightened concerns over potential disruptions in one of the world’s most critical oil shipping routes. The dollar index also moved higher, reflecting a shift toward safe-haven assets.    The risk-off sentiment was visible across global markets, with Europe’s Stoxx 600 index declining about 1 percent, extending losses after the reports emerged.    The sharp reversal in futures comes after a positive start to the session, when US contracts were pointing higher following strong momentum in global equities. Earlier in the day, Nasdaq 100 futures had risen about 0.3 percent and S&amp;amp;P 500 futures were up 0.1 percent, supported by optimism around AI-driven growth and better-than-expected earnings from megacap technology companies.    Investor sentiment had remained resilient in recent weeks despite ongoing geopolitical tensions, with global equities rallying for more than a month. US markets, in particular, have been supported by strong corporate earnings, with the S&amp;amp;P 500 notching five consecutive weeks of gains and a relatively low proportion of companies missing analyst estimates.    However, the latest developments around the Strait of Hormuz -- a key artery for global oil shipments -- have triggered a swift reassessment of risk, dragging equity futures lower while pushing energy prices higher. Shortly before, Tasnim, another Iranian news agency, announced the government had “redefined the control zone” in the Strait of Hormuz and effectively set out maritime borders within which Tehran would regulate shipping traffic. articles.title: SEBI chief says CKYC 2.0 to launch in July, unified KYC critical for financial sector
articles.snippet: SEBI chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said creating a unified KYC system is a top priority, with C-KYC 2.0 launching by July.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: SEBI chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said creating a unified KYC system is a top priority, with C-KYC 2.0 launching by July.
articles.body: The SEBI chair Tuhin Kanta Pandey, speaking at the IMC Capital Markets Conference, noted that a key priority for the regulator is the creation of a unified know-your-customer framework across the financial system.    Backing the government’s “One Nation, One KYC” vision, Pandey said the goal is to make onboarding seamless while ensuring data integrity. “What we really want is to have one KYC across the financial sector,” he said, adding that authentication remains the biggest challenge. Without reliable verification, pooled data risks becoming “untrustworthy,” he noted, calling for tighter coordination among regulators to build a robust, interoperable system.    Indian citizens should have an improved experience of financial services, with a seamless, secure, and a portable KYC experience across the financial sector, Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman had said last week, speaking at the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) 38th Foundation Day celebration.    &quot;I would suggest SEBI should help drive the prescription of the common KYC norms and the simplification and digitization of KYC processes across the Indian securities market,&quot; she added, since SEBI has &quot;a scale of investor participation, the depth of digital infrastructure, and the institutional credibility among peer regulators to take the lead in this domain.&quot; Sitharaman also encouraged all other regulators to work towards it with a &quot;sense of urgency.&quot;    To that extent, the market regulator is preparing C-KYC 2.0, which shall be launched by July. &quot;This is a very, very good opportunity for us to achieve what we have been aspiring for some time: one CKYC infrastructure.&quot;    On FPI flows, while Pandey acknowledged concerns around recent outflows, he said that global investors allocate capital based on risk-return considerations across markets. “They are looking at the world as a market, not India in isolation,” he said. While SEBI has taken steps to ease registration and improve market structure, flows will ultimately depend on global factors, sectoral opportunities and post-tax returns.    Further, Pandey said that foreign investors may look towards adding allocation towards sectors that are not as present in India, alluding to the Artificial Intelligence (AI) or semiconductor themes. However, he added that those sectors are also getting &quot;built up&quot; in India, which may lead to the return of foreign flows.    On disclosures, Pandey defended SEBI’s disclosure-based regime as the backbone of investor protection, but acknowledged the need for simplification. He pointed to the introduction of “abridged prospectuses” aimed at making key information more accessible to retail investors. “All core information should be encapsulated in a concise format,” he said, while allowing more detailed filings for institutional investors and foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), whose requirements differ. articles.title: Ambuja Cements Q4 consol net profit falls to Rs 569 cr after adjusting for one-offs; revenue hits record...
articles.snippet: Ambuja Cements Q4 PAT fell to Rs 569 crore from Rs 856 crore YoY, while quarterly revenue hit a record Rs 10,915 crore, up 9 percent YoY. EBITDA margins dropped to 13.4 percent due to higher costs.
articles.author: Shaleen Agrawal
articles.description: Ambuja Cements Q4 PAT fell to Rs 569 crore from Rs 856 crore YoY, while quarterly revenue hit a record Rs 10,915 crore, up 9 percent YoY. EBITDA margins dropped to 13.4 percent due to higher costs.
articles.body: Ambuja Cements Ltd reported a 33 percent fall in its normalised consolidated net profit for Q4 FY26, to Rs 569 crore from Rs 856 crore a year ago, even as its reported PAT (profit after tax) was elevated by one-time tax-related gains.    The cement major’s reported consolidated net profit rose 37 percent at Rs 1,857 crore for the quarter, up from Rs 1,351 crore a year earlier. The significant rise was largely due to one-off items, particularly tax reversals and deferred tax credits arising from recent mergers.    According to Ambuja Cements' investor presentation, the quarter included a substantial reversal of income tax provisions and deferred tax credit benefits linked to the merger of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement. These mergers enabled the utilisation of accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation, resulting in tax shields and a reversal of prior-period tax provisions.    The normalised profit was arrived at after adjusting for these and other one-offs -- including stamp duty, provisions, and litigation-related items.    Revenue for the quarter rose 9 percent year-on-year to Rs 10,915 crore from Rs 9,981 crore, supported by a 10 percent increase in sales volumes to 19.9 million tonnes.    However, operating performance weakened during the quarter. EBITDA declined 22 percent to Rs 1,464 crore from Rs 1,868 crore a year ago, while margins contracted sharply to 13.4 percent from 18.7 percent.    The margin compression was driven by cost pressures, particularly higher fuel and energy costs. The investor presentation (page 5) highlighted a sharp rise in petcoke prices during the quarter, along with packaging constraints and labour-related disruptions, which weighed on profitability.    Despite the pressure on earnings, the company reported its highest-ever quarterly sales volume and revenue, aided by improved realisations and a higher share of trade and premium products.    Looking ahead, Ambuja expects cost pressures to persist in the near term, with the impact of the West Asia conflict likely to continue into the first half of FY27. Demand growth is expected to remain moderate at around 5 percent, even as long-term infrastructure-led growth prospects remain intact.    Separately, on a standalone basis, the company had reported a sharp jump in net profit to Rs 1,644 crore from Rs 555 crore a year ago, aided by a tax credit of Rs 1,462 crore. Standalone revenue rose 5.5 percent to Rs 6,972 crore, while EBITDA declined 38.6 percent to Rs 646.5 crore, with margins contracting to 9.3 percent from 16 percent year-on-year. articles.title: RBI, IRDAI reluctant to allow banks and insurers into commodity derivatives, says SEBI chief
articles.snippet: RBI, IRDAI say ‘not the right time’ for banks, insurers in commodity derivatives, leading the SEBI chief said the markets regulator will not pursue the matter further with the other regulators.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: RBI, IRDAI say ‘not the right time’ for banks, insurers in commodity derivatives, leading the SEBI chief said the markets regulator will not pursue the matter further with the other regulators.
articles.body: India’s push to broaden participation in commodity derivatives markets has hit a pause, with key financial regulators opting to stay on the sidelines for now. Speaking at the IMC Capital Markets Conference, Tuhin Kanta Pandey, chairman of Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said both the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) have reservations about allowing banks and insurance companies to participate in commodity derivatives trading.    The capital markets regulator had earlier indicated it would engage with policymakers to explore widening the investor base in commodities, including permitting banks and pension funds to enter the segment. However, those discussions have not translated into regulatory support.    “They were engaged with them and they had their rationale that at this moment they do not feel it is the right time,” Pandey said, underscoring the cautious stance taken by both the banking and insurance regulators.    A key concern is the suitability of such instruments for certain financial institutions. Pandey pointed out that commodity derivatives may not align with the core investment strategies of insurers. “Commodity derivatives don’t make much sense for insurance firms, which typically focus on long-term investments,” he noted.    He added that the pension sector regulator has also examined the possibility of allowing pension funds to invest in commodities, though he did not indicate whether any decision had been reached.    For now, SEBI is unlikely to push the proposal further. “They have their rationale… we will leave it here,” Pandey said, suggesting that any expansion of participation in commodity derivatives will have to wait until broader regulatory consensus emerges. articles.body: Shares of Godrej Properties Ltd jumped as much as 6.3 percent intraday on Monday after the company reported a strong set of Q4 results, but soon shed most of the gains. articles.title: LSG owner RPSG Ventures' shares rise 5% as Lakshmi Mittal, Poonawalla-led group to buy Rajasthan Royals...
articles.snippet: The RPSG group acquired the Lucknow franchise for Rs 7,090 crore in November 2021. The franchise is held through RPSG Sports Private Limited
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The RPSG group acquired the Lucknow franchise for Rs 7,090 crore in November 2021. The franchise is held through RPSG Sports Private Limited
articles.body: Shares of RPSG Ventures, owner of IPL franchise Lucknow Super Giants, rose 5% on May 4 after a consortium led by steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and vaccine tycoon Adar Poonawalla has agreed to acquire Indian Premier League franchise Rajasthan Royals in a deal valuing the team at Rs 15,600 crore.    Mittal will hold about 75% of the franchise along with his family, while Poonawalla is set to own around 18%, a statement issued by the consortium said. Existing investors, including Manoj Badale, will retain about a 7% stake.    The deal includes the Rajasthan Royals' men's IPL team as well as its sister franchises Paarl Royals in South Africa's SA20 competition and Barbados Royals in the Caribbean Premier League.    Completion of the transaction is subject to regulatory approval, including from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), the antitrust watchdog and the IPL Governing Council, and is expected in the third quarter of 2026.    Mittal, his son Aditya, and daughter Vanisha Mittal-Bhatia, Poonawalla and Badale will join the Rajasthan Royals' board following completion.    Badale will continue to support the franchise in an ongoing role.    In March, a consortium comprising the Aditya Birla Group, Times of India Group, Bolt Ventures and Blackstone said it would buy IPL franchise RCB from United Spirits for $1.78 billion.    Key factors driving investor interest in the league are a doubling in the value of broadcast rights to more than $6 billion in the most recent auction in 2022, rising franchise revenues and the Indian cricket board BCCI's pooled revenue-sharing model that bolsters team revenues.    Earlier in March, Moneycontrol reported, citing sources, that Sanjiv Goenka-led RPSG group has joined the bandwagon of IPL franchise owners looking to monetise their cricket teams, with plans to sell a minority stake in Lucknow Super Giants (LSG). Goenka is exploring a sale of up to 15 percent, sources said.    The RPSG group acquired the Lucknow franchise for Rs 7,090 crore in November 2021. The franchise is held through RPSG Sports Private Limited.    In H1 FY26, the IPL franchise reported a revenue of Rs 495.9 crore and a profit of Rs 63.7 crore.    The report said FY25 moderated by 20% to Rs 557 crore, mainly due to lower number of matches played in the year, and lower ranking of LSG in IPL season 2024, compared to 2023.

articles.body: Adani Ports &amp;amp; SEZ Ltd shares surged on Monday, gaining about 5 percent in late morning trade, as investors reacted to the company’s strong Q4 FY26 financial results, bullish brokerage commentary, and a fresh operational update showing robust cargo growth for April. The stock was trading at Rs 1,741, strongly gaining after ending marginally down in the previous session. On Thursday, Adani Ports stock slipped 0.23 percent post results. Markets were shut on Friday.    The latest trigger came from the company’s April operational update, where Adani Ports reported a 15 percent year-on-year rise in cargo volumes to 43.1 million metric tonnes (MMT). The growth was driven by containers and dry cargo, both of which grew 17 percent on-year. However, logistics rail volumes declined 16 percent to 48,490 TEUs during the month.    The stock reaction also builds on a strong set of Q4 numbers. Adani Ports reported a 10.4 percent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,329 crore, while revenue grew 26.5 percent to Rs 10,737 crore. articles.title: Sun TV stock falls 8% to emerge as top mid-cap loser amid Vijay-led TVK's massive gains in Tamil Nadu:...
articles.snippet: New entrant TVK, led by actor-politician Vijay, was leading in as many as 98 constituencies on Monday when counting of votes polled in the April 23 Assembly polls was on across Tamil Nadu
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: New entrant TVK, led by actor-politician Vijay, was leading in as many as 98 constituencies on Monday when counting of votes polled in the April 23 Assembly polls was on across Tamil Nadu
articles.body: Shares of Sun TV Network fell 8% on May 4 to emerge as top mid-cap loser as the ruling DMK was trailing behind the Vijay-led TVK, with AIADMK in second position.    As of May 2026, Sun TV Network, founded by Kalanithi Maran, has historically been closely affiliated with the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party, given the Maran brothers are grand-nephews of the late DMK patriarch M Karunanidhi.    At 10:40 am on May 4, Sun TV shares were trading 8% lower at Rs 557.65 apiece. The stock recorded its sharpest single-day fall since August 2024.    New entrant TVK, led by actor-politician Vijay, was leading in as many as 98 constituencies on Monday when counting of votes polled in the April 23 Assembly polls was on across Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK was leading in 74 seats while the ruling DMK was ahead in 61, EC data showed.    About two hours after the postal ballots were counted and EVMs opened for multi-round counting, Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam surged ahead of its Dravidian rivals-- the DMK and the AIADMK, with the ruling party struggling to catch up.    If the trends maintain, Vijay could as well ensure the biggest electoral upset, something in lines with the &quot;1967,1977&quot; wins he had referred to in his campaign speeches.    While the Dravidian stalwart CN Annadurai brought the first non-Congress government in Tamil Nadu post-independence in 1967, the charismatic MG Ramachandran (MGR) installed the maiden AIADMK government 10 years later, unseating then DMK government under M Karunanidhi. TVK was leading in most Chennai segments, all considered DMK strongholds and currently represented by the party in the 234-member House.    A poor show by DMK could belie most exit polls giving an edge to it, riding on the number of populist measures Chief Minister M K Stalin had implemented in his five year &quot;Dravidian model,&quot; inclusive governance.    According to EC and TV reports, 15 cabinet ministers, including Stalin were trailing. His son and deputy CM Udhayanidhi was also behind in his incumbent Chepauk-Tirvuvallikeni seat, according to a number of reports.    Stalin was trailing behind TVK's VS Babu by 1234 votes in Kolathur segment. Vijay was ahead in Tiruchirappalli East by over 3,000 votes at the end of two rounds of counting, according to EC data.    BJP is trailing in 26 constituencies and it is ahead in Thali segment alone. TVK is ahead in constituencies including Ponneri, Tiruvallur, Poonamalle, and Avadi.

The rally was supported by April auto sales data, easing crude prices and positive political cues.    2) Persistent FII selling: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) continued to offload equities, selling shares worth Rs 8,047.86 crore on Thursday, which weighed on sentiment.    3) BJP likely Bengal win doesn't enthuse markets: Despite BJP's likely BJP win in West Bengal, markets are looking for cues from US-Iran war, said an analyst. Oil was close to $113 a barrel, with the Brent crude oil futures contract having rolled over to the July 2026 contract.    The United States President Donald Trump said his country may help guide neutral ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could ease supply concerns slightly.    Brent prices have consistently stayed above $100 a barrel. A lack of progress on a definitive peace plan between the US and Iran has kept traders on the sidelines.    On April 30, Brent crossed $120 a barrel, which sent the rupee and bonds in a tailspin.    Markets are stuck between fear and hope, and that confusion is reflected in currencies and fixed income, traders said.    Higher Brent is detrimental to the country’s inflation outlook, and will continue to pressure domestic bond yields.    The rupee opened four paise lower on May 4, at 94.95 a dollar after ending the previous session at 94.91. The rupee fell to an all-time low on April 30 at 95.33 after Brent briefly hit a $120 a barrel. Currency and fixed income markets were closed on May 1.

articles.title: Vedanta shares rebound 6% today after ex-demerger drop; stock recovers post-adjustment losses
articles.snippet: The recovery in Vedanta’s share price today comes after a phase of profit-booking and technical adjustments ahead of the demerger record date.
articles.author: Shaleen Agrawal
articles.description: The recovery in Vedanta’s share price today comes after a phase of profit-booking and technical adjustments ahead of the demerger record date.
articles.body: Vedanta Ltd shares rebounded sharply in early trade on Monday, rising over 6 percent to Rs 288.75, recovering most of the losses seen after last week’s ex-demerger adjustment.    The stock had adjusted downward on Thursday following a special pre-open session that reset its price to Rs 289.5 on an ex-demerger basis. Soon after the adjustment, the stock had slipped further during the session to close more than 6 percent lower. Monday’s recovery indicates stabilisation after the technical price adjustment triggered by the restructuring.    Vedanta shares are now trading close to their post-demerger discovery price, with traders likely dismissing any fundamental deterioration in the business.    The sharp decline last week had followed the separation of four key business verticals -- aluminium, power, oil &amp;amp; gas, and steel -- into independent entities. As a result, the adjusted share price reflects only the residual Vedanta business, which is anchored by Hindustan Zinc.    Under the demerger scheme, shareholders will receive one share each in the four newly created companies for every share held in Vedanta Ltd as of the record date. The value of these entities is expected to be unlocked separately once they are listed, likely over the coming months.    Brokerages have maintained a constructive view on the restructuring, citing potential value unlocking as a key catalyst. Emkay Global said the transition to pure-play entities could lead to valuation re-rating, supported by improved capital allocation and focused management teams. The brokerage also highlighted that aluminium and zinc continue to be the primary earnings drivers, contributing a bulk of profitability.    Analysts have also pointed to the company’s balance sheet restructuring as a positive, with debt being aligned to the cash flow profiles of individual businesses. Oil &amp;amp; gas and iron &amp;amp; steel entities are expected to be largely net-debt free, while leverage across other segments remains proportionate to their earnings capacity.    The recovery in Vedanta’s share price comes after a phase of profit-booking and technical adjustments ahead of the demerger record date. With the initial volatility settling, market participants are now expected to shift focus to the listing timelines and valuation of the demerged entities, which are seen as key triggers for further price discovery. articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares rise 4.5% as govt trims telco's AGR dues by 27%
articles.snippet: DoT has slashed AGR liability on debt-ridden Vodafone Idea by about 27% to Rs 64,046 crore after reassessment of statutory dues
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: DoT has slashed AGR liability on debt-ridden Vodafone Idea by about 27% to Rs 64,046 crore after reassessment of statutory dues
articles.body: Shares of Vodafone Idea rose 4.5% on May 5 after the government has slashed adjusted gross revenue liability on debt-ridden Vodafone Idea by about 27% to Rs 64,046 crore after reassessment of statutory dues.    The Department of Telecom (DoT) has frozen the AGR dues as on December 31, 2025, at Rs 87,695 crore and that the said amount was, however, subject to reassessment by the DoT and final approval by a Committee to be constituted by the DoT to reassess the AGR dues.    At 9:40 am on May 5, Vodafone Idea shares were trading 4% higher at Rs 10.65 apiece.    &quot;We now wish to submit that the DoT vide its communication dated 30 April 2026 has informed that the Committee formed for the purpose has finalised the AGR dues at Rs 64,046 crore as on 31 December 2025,&quot; Vodafone Idea said in a stock exchange filing on April 30.    The company has to clear final dues in two sets spread over a period of ten years. It will need to pay a minimum of Rs 100 crore annually over four years from FY 2031-32 to FY 2034-35 and the remaining amount in six equal instalments annually from FY 2035-36 to FY 2040-41, the filing said.

articles.title: Sensex gains 350 pts, Nifty above 24,100: BJP's poll show among key factors behind market rise
articles.snippet: Sensex, Nifty rose as auto shares led the gains on strong monthly sales data.
articles.author: Paras Bisht
articles.description: Sensex, Nifty rose as auto shares led the gains on strong monthly sales data.
articles.body: The benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty settled higher on Monday, supported by easing crude oil prices, firm global cues and buying in auto shares.    The Sensex climbed 355.90 points or 0.46 percent to settle at 77,269.40. During the day, it jumped 997.25 points or 1.29 percent to 77,910.75. The Nifty rallied 121.75 points or 0.51 percent to end at 24,119.30.    Shares of Maruti Suzuki India surged 4 percent after the company reported total sales of 2,39,646 units in April, registering a 33.29 percent year-on-year growth.    All 16 major sectoral indices traded in the green. The broader Nifty smallcap100 and midcap100 indices rose about 1 percent each.    Among individual stocks, Hindustan Unilever gained 3.7 percent after reporting a rise in March-quarter profit, aided by consumption tax cuts. Equitas Small Finance Bank jumped 9.6 percent following a surge in quarterly profit.    NCC Ltd rose 2 percent after securing four orders worth Rs 1,703 crore in April. However, Kotak Mahindra Bank declined 2.7 percent amid concerns over margin outlook due to rising deposit costs in the coming fiscal.  Key factors behind market rise  1) State election results: State poll results moved towards an outcome in line with market expectations.    &quot;Investor sentiment remained supported by a favourable election outcome in West Bengal and a better-than-expected Q4 earnings, helping markets look past Middle East-related concerns,&quot; Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited, said.    2) Crude oil prices decline: Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, was trading 0.27 percent lower at USD 107.9 per barrel, after touching a four-year high of USD 126.41 last week.    &quot;President Donald Trump’s declaration that the US will help and guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz has brought Brent crude down to around USD 108 levels. Also, there is a latest proposal from Iran to the US delivered through Pakistan,&quot; Vijayakumar added. He said crude oil prices and developments in West Asia would continue to guide market trends.  Stock Market Live Updates  3) Firm trends in global markets: Asian markets, including South Korea’s Kospi, China’s Shanghai SSE Composite and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng, were trading higher, while US markets ended mostly in the green on Friday.    4) Strong buying in auto shares: The auto index rose about 2 percent, leading sectoral gains. Shares of Hero MotoCorp and Maruti Suzuki gained 2.3 percent and 4 percent, respectively, on strong monthly sales data. Bajaj Auto jumped 4.8 percent to an 18-month high after reporting a 40 percent year-on-year rise in April sales.    5) Easing geo-political concerns: Geopolitical concerns eased after the US indicated steps to help free ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz.    &quot;While there could be a significant delay in finding a full-fledged solution to the Iran war, resumption of major attacks between the US and Iran looks more unlikely, lending stability to markets,&quot; G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomics Research told Reuters.  Technical Outlook   Anand James, Chief Market Strategist at Geojit Investments, said Friday’s doji formation with a long lower wick indicates attempts by bulls to regain momentum. He said the Nifty could move towards the 25,000–25,600 range, though volatility may persist with the VIX above 18. The immediate breakout range for the index is seen at 24,050–24,350. articles.title: Rupee opens 4 paise lower at 94.95 against the dollar, Brent still a worry
articles.snippet: The rupee had fallen to an all-time low of 95.33 on April 30 after Brent crude rose to $120 a barrel
articles.author: Archishma Iyer
articles.description: The rupee had fallen to an all-time low of 95.33 on April 30 after Brent crude rose to $120 a barrel
articles.body: The rupee opened four paise lower on May 4, as traders remained cautious even after Brent crude slipped over the weekend after US President Donald Trump said the America would guide stranded ships out of the Strait of Hormuz.    The rupee was trading at 94.95 a dollar after ending the previous session at 94.91. The rupee fell to an all-time low on April 30 at 95.33 after Brent briefly hit a $120 a barrel. Currency and fixed income markets were closed on May 1.    The rupee has remained under pressure in recent sessions, sliding nearly 2 percent over the past eight trading days, Reuters said.    The sustained weakness reflects a feedback loop from high oil prices, which has eroded ​sentiment, prompted heavier ⁠hedging by importers and reinforced steady dollar demand from oil refiners, it added.    The benchmark Brent was trading at near $108, with the Brent crude oil futures contract having rolled over to the July contract.    Trump said the US may help guide neutral ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could ease supply concerns slightly. Trump, however, didn’t share the details of the plan even as peace efforts with Iran remain deadlocked.    Brent has remained above $100, pushing the rupee on back foot. The lack of progress on a peace plan between the US and Iran has kept traders on the sidelines.    Domestically, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) likely intervened in the market after the rupee hit an all-time low, and will likely keep the rupee under check from any further free-fall, according to traders.    Higher Brent crude prices are detrimental to the country’s import bill and current account deficit, and pressure the rupee.    “Right now, the rupee is standing at a critical zone — not just technically, but psychologically. The 95.20–95.30 range is expected to act as a strong resistance in the near term,” Amit Pabari, managing director at CR Forex Advisors, said.

articles.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank stock falls 2.6%, top Nifty loser; analysts hail Q4 results margin gains, but flag RoE...
articles.snippet: Kotak Mahindra Bank’s asset quality improved during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets easing sequentially, while provisions declined sharply, supporting earnings.
articles.author: Shaleen Agrawal
articles.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank’s asset quality improved during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets easing sequentially, while provisions declined sharply, supporting earnings.
articles.body: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares fell on Monday even after the lender reported Q4 FY26 results that beat expectations. Brokerages highlighted margin gains and improved asset quality, but flagged relatively weaker return ratios.    In the morning trade, Kotak Mahindra Bank stock was trading at Rs 373.35, down 2.6 percent on the day. The stock has declined about 10.5 percent over the past one year, compared with a roughly 1 percent fall in the Nifty 50 over the same period.    The private sector lender reported a 13.4 percent year-on-year rise in net profit at Rs 4,026.55 crore for the March quarter, beating Bloomberg estimates. Net interest income (NII) rose 8.1 percent on-year to Rs 7,876 crore.    Operating profit increased 7 percent year-on-year to Rs 5,855 crore. Interest income grew 4.8 percent to Rs 14,175 crore, while interest expense rose just 0.9 percent to Rs 6,299 crore. Other income declined 2.1 percent to Rs 3,116 crore. Margins showed improvement on a sequential basis, with net interest margin at 4.67 percent for the quarter, compared with 4.54 percent in the previous quarter, although lower than 4.97 percent a year ago.    Asset quality strengthened during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets easing to 1.20 percent from 1.30 percent quarter-on-quarter. Net NPAs declined to 0.25 percent from 0.31 percent. Provisions fell sharply by 36 percent sequentially to Rs 516 crore, supporting profitability.    Loan growth remained healthy, with net advances rising 16 percent year-on-year to about Rs 4.96 lakh crore, while deposits grew 15 percent to around Rs 5.72 lakh crore.    Brokerage firm Bernstein maintained a ‘market perform’ rating on Kotak Mahindra Bank stock with a target price of Rs 500 per share. It said that the bank delivered a strong quarter with broad-based performance. The brokerage highlighted that net interest margins expanded and credit costs declined on the back of improved asset quality, while loan growth remained healthy. However, Bernstein flagged that return on equity continues to lag peers.    UBS retained a ‘buy’ rating with a target price of Rs 500 per share. It said that the profit beat was driven by higher pre-provision operating profit and lower credit costs. The brokerage said improving asset quality and stable margins support valuations. articles.body: Indian markets are set to open higher on Monday, tracking gains in GIFT Nifty, which was up 112 points or 0.46 percent at 24,259 in early trade, indicating a positive start for benchmark indices after Thursday’s weak close.    The improved opening cues come as crude oil prices eased from recent highs, offering some relief to global risk sentiment. Brent crude futures fell 64 cents, or 0.59 percent, to $107.53 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate slipped 84 cents, or 0.82 percent, to $101.10, after sharp gains last week driven by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the pullback, crude remains elevated above the $100 mark, keeping inflation concerns alive.    Global cues were supportive. Asian markets traded higher in early deals, with MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rising 0.6 percent, while South Korea’s Kospi surged 2.6 percent on return from a holiday. Japan markets were shut, leading to relatively thin volumes, though Nikkei futures edged up to 59,630 from the previous close of 59,513.    On Wall Street, equities ended mixed on Friday, with the S&amp;amp;P 500 rising 21.11 points, or 0.29 percent, to close at a record 7,230.12, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 222.13 points, or 0.89 percent, to 25,114.44. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, slipped 152.87 points, or 0.31 percent, to 49,499.27.    Back home, investors are closely watching state election outcomes, particularly in West Bengal, where counting is underway. While state elections typically do not alter long-term market direction, any deviation from expectations could trigger near-term volatility.    Institutional flows remain a key monitorable. Foreign institutional investors extended their selling streak for the ninth consecutive session on Thursday, offloading over Rs 8,000 crore worth of equities, while domestic institutional investors remained net buyers with inflows of Rs 3,487 crore, helping cushion the downside.    Technical analysts say markets may remain range-bound despite the positive start, with crude oil prices, geopolitical developments, currency movement, and election outcomes likely to dictate intraday direction. The Nifty continues to face resistance around the 24,300–24,400 zone, while immediate support is seen near the 23,800 level. articles.title: Chartist Talk: Ashish Kyal explains why investors should focus on mid-cap and small-cap stocks in coming...
articles.snippet: According to Ashish Kyal, the next few days of price action in the Nifty 50 will be crucial, with a high probability that a major bottom is already in place.
articles.author: Sunil Shankar Matkar
articles.description: According to Ashish Kyal, the next few days of price action in the Nifty 50 will be crucial, with a high probability that a major bottom is already in place.
articles.body: Ashish Kyal, the Founder and CEO of Waves Strategy Advisors believes both mid-cap and small-cap indices appear well-positioned to retest their lifetime highs and continue outperforming the Nifty in the coming months.    Hence, investors should focus on mid-cap and small-cap stocks that are emerging as near-term leaders, he advised.    According to him, the next few days of price action in the Nifty 50 will be crucial, with a high probability that a major bottom is already in place. &quot;Time cycle analysis indicates that May 27 will be an important period, post which upside momentum is expected to pick up, he said in an interview to Moneycontrol.    Do you think small- and mid-cap stocks are completely back in action? Will they record better gains than large-cap stocks from here on?    Mid-cap and small-cap indices have been outperforming the Nifty even during the market decline in March and April, a trend that has largely gone unnoticed. A ratio analysis of the mid-cap index to the Nifty, as well as the small-cap index to the Nifty, clearly highlights this strong outperformance. This suggests that the broader market remained relatively stable compared to the large-cap index, which witnessed significant selling pressure.    More recently, the Nifty Midcap 100 is just about 3 percent below its lifetime high, whereas the Nifty remains around 9 percent below its peak. Additionally, the small-cap index has surged nearly 20 percent from its lows on March 23, compared to an 8 percent rise in the Nifty over the same period.    Both mid-cap and small-cap indices therefore appear well-positioned to retest their lifetime highs and continue outperforming the Nifty in the coming months, indicating that investors should focus on mid-cap and small-cap stocks that are emerging as near-term leaders.    Are the charts signalling that a bottom has been formed in the Nifty 50?    The Nifty 50 has shown upward momentum since April 2. After forming a high near 24,600, some short-term profit booking has been observed. articles.title: Global oil faces 4.8 mbpd supply gap as demand destruction seen capping prices
articles.snippet: Global oil faces a 4.8 mbpd supply gap after Hormuz disruptions, but demand destruction may cool prices, PL Capital says.
articles.author: ANI
articles.description: Global oil faces a 4.8 mbpd supply gap after Hormuz disruptions, but demand destruction may cool prices, PL Capital says.
articles.body: A supply deficit of around 4.8 million barrels per day (mbpd) in the global oil market is expected to be absorbed through demand destruction amid ongoing disruptions in West Asia, according to a report by PL Capital.    The report said the conflict in West Asia has tightened global oil supply, leading to higher prices and increased volatility. The disruption of crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz has resulted in a supply loss of nearly 15 mbpd.  However, part of this loss has been offset by strategic releases of about 400 million barrels (mb) by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the use of alternative export routes bypassing Hormuz, which account for around 6.2 mbpd. Despite these measures, a gap of about 4.8 mbpd remains in the market.    It stated, &quot;Supply deficit of 4.8mbpd needs to be compensated.... Against a supply balance of ~4.8mbpd, such expected demand destruction will partially rebalance market dynamics further, putting a downward pressure on crude prices&quot;.  The report noted that this imbalance is expected to be addressed through demand destruction as higher oil prices begin to weigh on consumption globally.    Early signs of demand slowdown are already visible. The IEA expects global oil demand to contract by around 1.5 mbpd in the second quarter of 2026, with a sharper decline of about 2.3 mbpd in April 2026, compared to industry estimates of around 4.0 mbpd.    The demand slowdown is initially expected to be concentrated in the Middle East and Asia-Pacific regions. However, as supply tightness continues and prices remain elevated, the demand destruction is likely to spread across other regions as well.    The report added that governments in oil-consuming countries may introduce policy measures or mandates to curb consumption, which could further contribute to rebalancing the market over time.    The report said that as demand destruction continues and helps rebalance the market, it could eventually put downward pressure on crude prices.    In this context, PL Capital said it remains positive on oil marketing companies (OMCs) such as Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited.    It noted that a decline in crude prices driven by demand destruction is expected to improve marketing margins for these companies, although this could be partly offset by softer fuel demand volumes.

articles.author: Shishir Asthana
articles.description: A strong performance by the BJP in state elections can help improve market sentiment
articles.body: Dear Reader,    Indian equities closed nearly flat for the week as caution gripped the market. Stalled US–Iran diplomacy, a sharp surge in crude oil prices, persistent foreign institutional selling, and a rupee touching record lows all weighed on sentiment.    For the week, Nifty 50 edged up 99.6 points, or 0.41%, to settle at 23,997.55. The broader market did better, with the Nifty Midcap 100 bouncing back from the prior week's losses to finish 0.7 percent higher, and smallcap stocks gained 2.5 percent.    As for sector performance, Nifty Oil &amp;amp; Gas, IT, and Pharma each rallied roughly 3 percent during the week. IT stocks continued their recovery on the back of resilient commentary around technology spending.          The Indian rupee was the story of the week as it slid to a fresh record low of 95.33 against the US dollar on April 30 before staging a partial recovery to close at 94.92 — still 67 paise weaker than the previous week's 94.25. FIIs remained net sellers throughout the week, offloading equities worth Rs 13,771.50 crore.  Despite the turbulent week, both the Sensex and the Nifty delivered gains of roughly 7 percent each for the month — their strongest monthly performance since June 2024.  US equities also closed the month on a strong note with a gain of 10 percent, its highest monthly gain since November 2020. Strong corporate results more than offset the drag from rising commodity costs and a hawkish Fed commentary. Oil markets were volatile through the week, with a gain of 7 percent, especially after the UAE decided to come out of the OPEC cartel.  Going forward, Indian markets are expected to take cues from state election results on Monday and then follow the global trend for most of the week. A strong performance by the BJP in state elections can help improve market sentiment.  Consolidation expected  On the weekly timeframe, the Nifty settled at 23,997.55, registering a modest gain of 0.42 percent for the week. Price has been consistently respecting a long-standing ascending trendline that has served as a reliable floor across multiple touchpoints. In recent weeks, price dipped towards that trendline once again, found support, and rejected lower levels — a sign that underlying momentum remains constructive and that buyers continue to see value at these levels.  However, drawing a descending trendline from the recent swing highs reveals that price is now pressing against meaningful resistance from above, which happens to coincide with the 40-week exponential moving average. When price runs into this kind of confluence, it often triggers a period of consolidation or a measured pullback rather than an immediate breakout, and current price action appears to be reflecting exactly that. On the momentum front, the RMI has registered a bullish crossover, suggesting that despite near-term hesitation, the underlying bias is beginning to tilt in favour of the bulls. The broader structural trend on the higher timeframe remains intact, and once this corrective phase runs its course, the conditions for a resumption of the uptrend are likely to fall into place.        The FII net index position indicator currently reads at -1,84,476, showing a recovery from the extreme bearish levels seen earlier. The structure is now forming higher highs, indicating that FIIs are reducing their short positions and that selling pressure is gradually easing. A trendline drawn from the recent bottom further reinforces this view, with the pattern of higher highs and higher lows suggesting that FIIs are steadily closing or trimming their previous short positions. Taken together, these signals point towards an improving stance from FIIs.        The percentage of Nifty 50 stocks carrying a daily RMI buy signal, which serves as a breadth indicator, has fallen sharply from the extreme overbought territory of 80 to 90 down to a reading of just 20, placing it firmly in oversold conditions. Historically, such depressed readings — where the overwhelming majority of stocks are flashing sell signals and very few are showing any buying momentum — have tended to precede meaningful market turnarounds. When this indicator retreats to such an extreme low zone, it is often a sign that selling pressure is running out of steam, making a recovery or a sharp bounce increasingly probable in the sessions ahead.          Another breadth indicator worth watching is the percentage of Nifty 50 stocks trading above their 200-day simple moving average. A couple of weeks ago, this indicator was languishing in oversold territory, but it has since begun to turn higher, reflecting a growing number of stocks reclaiming that long-term moving average. This gradual improvement in participation is a healthy sign, suggesting that the positive momentum is not confined to a handful of index heavyweights, but is instead broadening out across the Nifty 50 basket — a development that typically underpins a more durable and sustainable uptrend.        Rounding out the breadth picture, the net new one-year highs indicator for Nifty 50 stocks has turned positive for the first time in nearly two months. Through that extended period, the indicator had remained in negative territory, meaning no stocks within the index were managing to register fresh one-year highs — a reflection of the broader corrective phase the market was working through. The shift to a positive reading is, therefore, a notable development, signalling that select Nifty 50 stocks are beginning to find their footing and are once again pushing towards new highs, adding another layer of evidence that the worst of the correction may well be behind us.    &amp;nbsp;        Sector Rotation  Nifty 50 – The Benchmark Index ended lower, by 0.42 percent this week and closed at 23,997,55.      Weekly RRG    Leading Quadrant   Nifty Metals and Nifty Energy are performing well, with momentum rising compared to last week, indicating likely continued outperformance. Nifty MNC and Nifty Media are also leading, but with flat momentum. Nifty Pharma, Consumer Durables, and PSE lead with slightly decreasing momentum while Nifty Infra has a sharper momentum drop. Finally, Nifty Oil &amp;amp; Gas is still in the leading quadrant, but its momentum is sharply declining and is expected to move towards the weakening quadrant. This makes it an important sector to keep an eye on as it may show weakness ahead.      Weakening Quadrant  Nifty PSU Banks is in the weakening quadrant with a steep drop in momentum visible. Nifty Bank and Nifty Private Banks are also weakening quickly with a reduction in momentum. Notably, Nifty Private Banks is on the verge of moving into the lagging quadrant, signalling likely underperformance. If the market continues to fall, Nifty Private Banks may present bearish opportunities. Nifty Auto is also in the weakening quadrant though this week has seen a slight improvement in momentum. If that recovery continues, Auto could shift back to the leading quadrant, making it a sector worth watching.  Improving Quadrant  Nifty IT has been in the lagging quadrant for the past two weeks. However, momentum is now sharply improving, and if it continues to rise, Nifty IT could shift towards the improving quadrant in the near future.          Lagging Quadrant        Nifty Realty and Nifty FMCG are gaining momentum sharply. Nifty Realty, which moved from lagging to improving in the past three weeks, is continuing to strengthen. Nifty FMCG is also showing a sharp momentum increase. If FMCG continues this momentum growth, it could move into the leading quadrant and outperform, especially if the overall market rallies.    Stocks to watch  Among the stocks expected to perform better during the week are MCX, Schneider, Power India, Nestle, GE Shipping, BSE, Aarti Industries, Karnataka Bank and Cummins India.    &amp;nbsp;    Cheers,     Shishir Asthana     &amp;nbsp;

articles.title: Daily Voice: Strait of Hormuz risks may hit rupee, input costs but not India’s resilience, says...
articles.snippet: According to Puneet Sharma, in the short term, there will be volatility and swings in the market. Therefore, the definition of a range-bound market is broader in this context.
articles.author: Sunil Shankar Matkar
articles.description: According to Puneet Sharma, in the short term, there will be volatility and swings in the market. Therefore, the definition of a range-bound market is broader in this context.
articles.body: The input costs will rise, and the falling rupee will add pressure due to risks related to the Strait of Hormuz. However, the economy is resilient enough, and the market is likely to shrug this off as well, said Puneet Sharma, CEO and Fund Manager at Whitespace Alpha, in an interview with Moneycontrol.    India has diversified its supply chain and is not solely dependent on the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, India and China are among the largest buyers of crude oil, and hence sellers are more likely to work with them, he believes.    According to him, in the short term, there will be volatility and swings in the market. Therefore, the definition of a range-bound market is broader in this context, he added.    Do you see a possibility of a resumption of conflict in West Asia, given Trump’s stance, or is it unlikely considering the potential impact on both economies, the global outlook, and US elections?    There is an ongoing blockade of Iranian ports which fits the classic definition of conflict. This is gunboat diplomacy. In terms of a macroeconomic environment for global commerce, bombs starting to drop will neither make it better not worse.    So to me, this is not a factor in determining the likelihood of normalcy returning.    What is the likelihood of a deal between the US and Iran?    The issue right now is that Iran does not have a unified voice to negotiate on its behalf and hence the lowest common denominator will prevail in a negotiation. This by default will make their stance hard. The US has power on its side and will be unwilling to back down in the absence of a sweetheart deal. So in the immediate term until further pain is felt, the likelihood is not high.    Do you expect an extended closure of the Strait of Hormuz to put economic growth and corporate earnings at risk in the upcoming quarters, including FY27?    India has diversified it's supply chain. We are not solely dependant on the Strait of Hormuz.    Also, India and China are among the largest buyers of crude and hence sellers will be more willing to work with them. Yes the input costs will go up and the falling rupee does put pressure but the economy is resilient enough and the market will shrug this off as well.    It is far scarier to be a Pakistan in this scenario than India.    If yes, does this imply that strong FII inflows are unlikely in the coming months?    FII inflows have been clearly impacted by rupee's weakness. I would like to see the economy open up futher and attract FDI as cutting rates in the short term is very difficult in an inflationary environment.    Do you expect inflation concerns and supply chain disruptions to keep the market range-bound?    There will be volatility and swings. So the definition of range-bound is broad here. Investors should be prepared to bear short term volatility and trading strategies will prioritize capital preservation.    Is the IT sector caught in a perfect storm? Has the outlook been impacted in both the short and long term?    These are the best brains in India. Not all companies will come out unscathed but some will grow exponentially as well. The sector as a whole just needs to up the value chain. But it will take some time before we see this as a bellweather.    Do you completely rule out a Fed funds rate cut in 2026? Also, is it unlikely that a new Fed Chair could secure FOMC majority support for rate cuts?    Large Rate cuts look highly unlikely. It is easier to maintain status quo than change things. Minor cuts even if they happen won't change things dramatically.    There are fractures even within republican lines now. This may not be their No.1 priority.    Which sector can provide the best support to a portfolio in this market environment?    Best thing to do here is pick a diversified portfolio as defensive bets are richly valued and more volatile sectors are what they are volatile!! articles.body: The benchmark indices fell by around seven-tenths of a percent on April 30, with further weakening in market breadth. The market needs to defend Friday's low in the upcoming sessions for stability, as a breach below it may allow bears to gain further strength. The daily, weekly, and monthly Relative Strength Index (RSI) is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.
